To: d.kerrigan@northmail.example
Replying to: m01
Cc: none
Subject: Re: Blister packs for my mother - new patient

Dear Mr Kerrigan,

Thank you for contacting Erindale Park Pharmacy. We would be pleased to welcome your mother and help with her medications as she returns home. I understand you would like everything arranged before her discharge on Thursday.

We prepare weekly blister packs containing seven days of medication, with up to four administration times each day. There is currently no charge for the packaging itself. The usual prescription and dispensing charges apply; Ontario Drug Benefit covers most eligible medication costs for seniors, although any applicable co-payments or items not covered would still be payable.

For delivery, our regular service is on Tuesdays and Fridays between 2 and 6 p.m., free within eight kilometres. Your mother’s building is within our delivery area. For her first packs, we can arrange either Saturday pickup or a one-off Saturday delivery before 1 p.m. Please let us know which you would prefer.

To transfer her prescriptions, please provide the name and address of her current pharmacy. We will also need her OHIP number; please call us with this rather than sending it by email. We will contact the pharmacy directly to arrange the transfer. She does not need to sign a transfer form.

The first blister packs take approximately 48 hours to prepare after we have received all her prescriptions, including both the hospital discharge prescriptions and the transfers. Please ask the hospital team to fax her discharge prescriptions to us early on Thursday. If all the necessary prescriptions are received then, we would expect to have her first packs ready on Saturday.

The packs will not be ready when she leaves hospital on Thursday. Before discharge, please confirm with the discharge team that she will have enough interim medication and that someone can help her with every dose until the packs are picked up or delivered on Saturday. This is particularly important given the new medications and the difficulties she has had keeping track of her pills.

I would be happy to arrange an evening call to go through her medication list with you. Before discussing her medications, however, we need Margaret’s permission. We record this using our signed Family Communication Consent form. This protects her privacy while allowing her to choose whom we may speak with about her care. She can sign it at pickup, or we can send it with the delivery driver. Once we have her signed consent, we can arrange a suitable time to speak.

I would also like to offer a MedsCheck medication review at her home during her first week back. This takes about 20 minutes and gives us an opportunity to review her discharge medications and answer questions together. I could visit on Monday or Tuesday after 6 p.m.; please let me know whether either evening would suit her.

My direct line is 905-555-0148, extension 2. I am in the store Monday to Friday, 9 a.m. to 6 p.m., and can arrange an evening conversation with you.

Kind regards,

Rania Haddad
Pharmacist
Erindale Park Pharmacy
